note: Week 2026-09-21 build. Run fired on schedule Sunday 9/20 ~9:00pm CT; entries are recorded at official SIP regular-session closes of Friday 2026-09-18 and open Monday 9/21. PRIOR WEEK (9/14-9/18) closed essentially FLAT: -11.46 realized (-0.02%), 3 of 12 names green. ILMN carried the entire book: +16.07% (+762.91) on S&P 500 inclusion effective 9/21 plus a guidance raise to $5.30-5.40 adjusted EPS - the single best position this book has held. GOOGL added +187.68 (+3.26%). Against that, MTB -5.22% (-300.48) was the worst: a hawkish hike is a margin benefit right up until the market starts pricing it as a credit problem, and regional banks were where that repricing landed. VRT -2.98%, HPE -2.14% and NEM -2.68% did the rest of the damage. The SCHW hedge worked in direction but not in size (-1.86%) - the hike was so fully priced that it was sold on the news. WHAT HAPPENED WEDNESDAY AND WHY IT REFRAMES EVERYTHING. The FOMC delivered the first hike since 2023, taking the funds range to 3.75-4.00%, and Chair Warsh's press conference was hawkish enough that the Dow lost 631 points (-1.21%) on the day. Futures now put roughly 57.6% odds on ANOTHER 25bp hike at the October meeting. The 10-year finished the week back at 5.00% after Kansas City Fed President Schmid defended further hikes on Friday against inflation still above 3%; the 2-year is at 4.75% and the 30-year at 5.34%. The Bank of Japan hiked to 1.25%. On the week the Nasdaq rose 0.7% while the Dow fell 1.7% and the Russell 2000 fell to -3.7% month-to-date - this is a tape that is paying for earnings power and punishing duration, leverage and small caps. THE THREE DATED EVENTS INSIDE THIS WINDOW. FIRST, TRUMP AND XI MEET IN WASHINGTON ON THURSDAY 9/24 - trade, tariffs, Taiwan, the Iran war and AI, with a possible extension of the bilateral truce that expires in November and a proposed mutual tariff cut covering about $30B of goods. SECOND, PRELIMINARY SEPTEMBER PMIs LAND WEDNESDAY 9/23, followed by jobless claims and August new-home sales Thursday and durable goods Friday - the first hard data the market gets to judge whether Warsh is hiking into a slowdown. THIRD, EARNINGS ARE THIN AND CONSUMER-FACING: AZO Tuesday, CTAS/PAYX/GIS Wednesday, DRI and COST Thursday. The book owns NONE of them. THE HARDEST NEW NUMBER IS BANK OF AMERICA'S. On 9/18 BofA raised its 2030 semiconductor TAM to $3.2 TRILLION from $2.7T and its US semiconductor CAGR to 18% from 14%, with memory sales going from $937B in 2026 to $1.8T in 2030 and wafer-fab equipment from $156B in 2026 (raised from $144B, +33% y/y) to $360B in 2030. Separately RBC reiterated Outperform on Micron with a $1,500 target, reporting DRAM contract prices tracking UP MORE THAN 20% quarter-over-quarter in calendar Q3 against its own ~10% forecast. The tape confirmed it on Friday: LRCX +5.1%, AMAT +4.1%, SNDK +7.3%, STX +5.4%, all on roughly 2x average volume, while semiconductors were the only industry group green in a red session. HOW THE BOOK IS BUILT. Technology (3) takes the memory/equipment cycle through three DIFFERENT links rather than three tickers of the same trade: MU at $1,015.80 (DRAM, RBC $1,500, earnings 9/30 so NO binary event inside this window, 19.1% below its June high), AMAT at $444.57 (equipment, closed AT the session high on 2.20x volume, 39.9% below its June high, 38x earnings), WDC at $441.36 (NAND/HDD, 2.18x volume, 18.2x earnings - the cheapest multiple in the book's technology sleeve). Industrials (3) is the power-and-oil leg: GEV at $940.33, where CEO Scott Strazik told Morgan Stanley's Laguna conference on 9/16 that the $176B backlog is tracking above $200B by early 2027, second-half contract commitments will EXCEED the prior 20-gigawatt guide and Q4 commitments will exceed Q3 - consensus target $1,187.83, earnings 10/21 outside the window; ETN at $424.77, which closed Friday AT its session high on 2.27x volume, the strongest single industrial signal on the tape; and UAL at $108.71, the book's short-oil expression. Financials (3) is rebuilt around VOLATILITY AND REGULATION rather than around net interest margin, because the NIM trade was sold on the news Wednesday: CME at $276.01 closed near its session high on 1.68x volume and is the one business that gets paid MORE the less certain the rate path is, with October now a live 57.6% coin flip; GS at $942.00 trades at 14.5x earnings, the cheapest multiple in the book, 18.4% below its July high; HOOD at $119.82 is the tokenization position - the SEC granted an innovation exemption enabling trading in tokenized stocks, Bitcoin cleared $80,000, and HOOD closed +5.6% off its open on 1.59x volume. Healthcare (2) is the defensive sleeve into Wednesday's PMIs: LLY at $1,152.93 closed near its session high on 1.83x volume, and ISRG at $393.33 rose 3.1% off its open on 2.06x volume, 34.9% below its January high with an Oppenheimer Outperform and $500 target live. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT AND WHY. GOOGL WAS NOT CARRIED FORWARD despite being the second-best position last week: it opened at $357.21, printed $359.44, and closed at $349.54 - within a dollar of the session low - on 47.6M shares against a 24.8M average. That is 1.92x volume DISTRIBUTION, and a 3.3% gain is not worth holding through it. DELL WAS NOT RE-BOUGHT for the same reason and worse: it made a fresh 52-week high at $595.51 on Friday and then closed at $568.06, reversing 4.6% off the high into the close. HPE closed at $60.76, below its $61.72 open. ILMN, the week's big winner, WAS SOLD AND NOT RE-BOUGHT: the S&P 500 inclusion that drove it is effective at Monday's open, which makes it a fully-priced-in catalyst by the time this book would own it, and index-add strength typically fades after the effective date. VRT WAS DROPPED - it closed at $249.39, below the $256.33 200-day the prior book explicitly bought as support, so the setup that justified it is broken. MTB WAS NOT RE-BOUGHT after a -5.2% week; adding to the book's biggest loser on a bounce is not the discipline. NEM WAS DROPPED even with gold at $4,358: it closed DOWN on 21.5M shares against an 8.5M average, which is 2.52x distribution, and XME was the worst industry group on the tape at -2.3%. ZERO ENERGY for a second week - WTI at $101.50 and Brent at $104.26 have both rolled over as Saudi Arabia routes crude around Hormuz by ship-to-ship transfer off Sohar, a durable supply workaround rather than a diplomatic coin flip, and UAL is how the book is positioned for it. ZERO CONSUMER - AZO printed a 52-week low at $2,815.00 on Friday, LOW printed one at $192.09, TJX printed one at $122.78 two sessions earlier, and COST sits 18.3% below its high with Oppenheimer publicly flagging a possible miss Thursday night; a retail complex making 52-week lows into a hawkish Fed is not where this book wants to be. BOEING WAS SCREENED AND REJECTED despite the summit: CEO Kelly Ortberg said on 9/16 that stabilising 737 MAX output is taking longer than expected AND explicitly downplayed expectations of a large Chinese order at the summit. LRCX was rejected only because it is the same trade as AMAT at a higher multiple (50x vs 38x). CAVEAT ON THE VOLUME READS: Friday 9/18 was September quad witching, which inflates volume market-wide, so every volume-confirmation figure in this book should be read as relative rank within that session rather than as a clean signal - the ratios were used to rank names against each other on the same day, not as standalone evidence. THE BOOK'S MAIN UNCOVERED RISK is that the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday produces an AI or semiconductor headline that cuts against the memory complex, because Technology is the largest sleeve at 26.0% and Friday's semiconductor bid is the single thesis holding three positions. There is no short and no hedge against it; that risk is carried in cash. 11 names, 88.1% deployed, 11.9% cash.

positions.name: Micron Technology
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/18 at $1,015.80 on 35.8M shares against a 24.9M 30-day average (1.44x). Two hard datapoints landed that session. RBC Capital reiterated Outperform with a $1,500 price target and reported DRAM contract prices tracking UP MORE THAN 20% quarter-over-quarter in calendar Q3, against its own ~10% forecast, attributing customer spec reductions to tight supply rather than cost. Separately Bank of America raised its 2030 semiconductor TAM to $3.2 trillion from $2.7 trillion and now models memory sales going from $937B in 2026 to $1.8 trillion by 2030. Crucially, Micron's fiscal Q4 report is 9/30 - OUTSIDE this window - so the position captures pre-earnings positioning with no binary event inside the hold. Roughly $44M of October-2 $1,000 calls were bought Friday morning.
positions.risks: 212% year-to-date and 478% over twelve months means an enormous amount of the cycle is already banked, and a $1.15 trillion market cap moves the whole complex when it turns. China's CXMT took 9.5% of global DRAM revenue in Q2 and is now reportedly building a NAND R&D line - a longer-dated competitive threat but a headline risk inside a week that contains the Trump-Xi summit. AI-slowdown fears drove the mid-week drawdown this name is bouncing from, and those fears are narrative-driven and can return without notice.
positions.driver: Largest position in the book: the cleanest expression of the week's hardest new number, in the one name where the catalyst is a contract price already moving rather than a forecast, and with the earnings event safely outside the window.

positions.name: Applied Materials
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/18 at $444.57, which was the session HIGH of $445.00, up 5.3% from a $422.14 open on 14.3M shares against a 6.5M 30-day average (2.20x) - the strongest close-on-high in the entire candidate set. The trigger is Bank of America's 9/18 note raising 2026 wafer-fabrication-equipment spend to $156 billion from $144 billion, a 33% year-over-year increase, and 2030 WFE to $360 billion, a 23% CAGR. DRAM equipment specifically is modelled at $61B in 2026 rising to $85B in 2027. Applied is the largest diversified equipment supplier and sits directly in that line item. It trades at 38.3x earnings, 39.9% BELOW its $739.67 high of 6/30, so unlike the server names last week the capex story is not yet in the price.
positions.risks: A 40% drawdown from a June high is not automatically a discount - semicap is the most cyclical link in the chain and the de-rating happened for a reason. China remains a material revenue exposure for equipment makers, which makes this the position most directly exposed to a bad Trump-Xi headline on Thursday. Friday was quad witching, so the 2.20x volume figure is inflated in absolute terms even though it ranked near the top of the tape. No company-specific event inside the window.
positions.driver: The equipment link of the memory chain, bought 40% off its own high on the strongest close-at-session-high in the book, on a forecast raise that is a direct revenue input rather than sentiment.

positions.name: Western Digital
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/18 at $441.36, up 3.4% from a $426.69 open, on 13.5M shares against a 6.2M 30-day average (2.18x) - the highest volume ratio among the memory names. Storage is the third link of the same cycle and the tightest: TrendForce expects NAND supply to stay tight until the second half of 2027 because manufacturers have prioritised DRAM and high-bandwidth memory capacity, while AI data centers keep absorbing solid-state and high-capacity drive output. At 18.2x trailing earnings this is the cheapest multiple in the book's technology sleeve by a wide margin - less than half AMAT's 38.3x - and it sits 44.8% below its $799.87 high of 6/18.
positions.risks: That 44.8% drawdown from a June high is the largest in the book and it is the position's central risk: the market de-rated this business violently and a one-week holder is buying into an unresolved downtrend rather than an established uptrend. CXMT's reported move into NAND is aimed squarely here. The stock also closed 1.7% below its own session high of $448.85, meaning it gave something back into the close - weaker than AMAT's close-at-high. Sized accordingly at 7.8%, the smallest of the three technology names.
positions.driver: Third and cheapest link of the memory cycle at 18x earnings, taken on the highest volume ratio in the complex, sized down to respect the drawdown it is bouncing inside of.

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/18 at $940.33 on 4.1M shares against a 2.3M 30-day average (1.82x), having run from $882.14 on Tuesday - up 6.6% on the week while the Dow fell 1.7%. The catalyst is dated and specific: at Morgan Stanley's 14th Annual Laguna Conference on Wednesday 9/16, CEO Scott Strazik said the $176 billion second-quarter order backlog is tracking to surpass $200 BILLION by early 2027, that second-half contract commitments are now running ABOVE the company's prior 20-gigawatt guidance, that Q4 commitments will exceed Q3, and that gas capacity additions grow 50% by the end of 2026. Power, not chips, is the binding physical constraint on AI deployment, and gas turbines are the only dispatchable baseload that can be ordered today. Consensus target is $1,187.83 and earnings are 10/21 - outside this window.
positions.risks: 20.9x trailing earnings on a business whose backlog converts over years, and GLJ Research initiated on 9/14 with a SELL and a $470 target - less than half the entry - against Bernstein's $1,298, which is an unusually wide dispersion and a sign the valuation is genuinely contested. It is the second industrial levered to the same AI-power theme as ETN, so the two correlate on any AI-capex de-rating. It is also 21.4% below its $1,195.94 high of 7/6 and has already moved 6.6% in five sessions, so some of the Laguna news is in the price.
positions.driver: The hardest order-book number available this weekend - a backlog guided above $200B and commitments guided above the prior gigawatt guide - in the one part of the AI buildout that physically cannot be accelerated.

positions.name: Eaton Corp.
positions.catalyst: The only position carried forward, and it earned it on Friday's tape rather than on last week's result. ETN closed at $424.77 against a session high of $425.34 - a close within 13 cents of the high - up 3.3% from a $411.42 open on 4.6M shares versus a 2.0M 30-day average (2.27x), the strongest volume-plus-close-on-high combination of any industrial screened. It holds the UBS Buy with a $515 target, 21% above the entry, on a Q3 margin inflection from pricing and execution, and it is named alongside Vertiv in Nvidia's sovereign-AI framing as a power-infrastructure beneficiary. It finished the prior week flat (-0.14%) in a week the book lost money, and sits 11.1% below its $478.00 high of 8/12 with no scheduled event in the window.
positions.risks: 43.2x earnings for an electrical-equipment manufacturer remains a growth multiple on a cyclical business. Paired with GEV this is two Industrials names betting on the same data-center power thesis, which is concentration rather than diversification. If Wednesday's PMIs show manufacturing rolling over under a 4.00% funds rate, electrical equipment is squarely in the path.
positions.driver: Held because Friday's close was the strongest technical signal in the industrial complex, not because it was held last week - a 2.27x volume close at the session high in a red tape.

positions.name: United Airlines Holdings
positions.catalyst: The oil thesis that justified this position last week has improved, not degraded. WTI closed Friday at $101.50 (-0.4%) and Brent at $104.26 (-0.5%), extending a mid-week retreat from a four-month high of $106 on Tuesday, and the reason is structural rather than diplomatic: Saudi Arabia is now making additional crude available to Asian refiners by ship-to-ship transfer just OUTSIDE Hormuz near Oman's Sohar port, using shuttle vessels to run the strait and load waiting tankers - a physical workaround that survives the next headline in a way a negotiated arrangement would not. Equity Clock's weekend note explicitly argues oil may be peaking and is inclined to book profits in energy. UAL closed at $108.71 near its $109.38 session high on 4.7M shares against 3.5M (1.32x), trades at 10.2x earnings and sits 21.7% below its $138.77 high of 6/30.
positions.risks: Jet fuel is the largest variable cost line but it is not the only one, and an airline is the most cyclical consumer-facing business in the index at exactly the moment the consumer complex is printing 52-week lows and the Fed is still hiking. Thursday's new-home sales and Wednesday's PMIs are both capable of repricing recession odds against this position. The Hormuz situation can re-escalate - only four commodity vessels were detected transiting on Thursday - and a renewed attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline, three of whose pumping stations are still under repair, puts Brent back through $110.
positions.driver: The book's short-oil expression, carried forward because the supply workaround that drove crude lower is physical infrastructure rather than a diplomatic meeting that can collapse over a weekend.

positions.name: CME Group
positions.catalyst: The deliberate replacement for last week's net-interest-margin trade, which was sold on the news Wednesday. CME does not need rates to go in a particular direction - it needs the path to be UNCERTAIN, and after Warsh's hawkish press conference the October meeting is priced at roughly 57.6% for another 25bp, which is close to a coin flip and the most volume-generative configuration there is for interest-rate futures and options. The 10-year moved 7bp on Friday alone on a single Kansas City Fed speech. CME closed at $276.01 against a $277.47 session high, up 1.5% from a $271.89 open, on 3.3M shares versus a 2.0M 30-day average (1.68x) - one of the few financials that closed green on a day XLF fell 0.2%. 23.4x earnings, 16.1% below its $329.16 high of 3/3.
positions.risks: 23.4x for an exchange is a full multiple and the business is a volume utility - if the October meeting resolves to near-certainty early in the week, the volatility premium in the thesis deflates. Exchanges are also structurally low-beta, so this position will lag badly if the summit produces a relief rally. There is no company event in the window, so this is a positioning trade rather than a catalyst trade.
positions.driver: The one business in the book that gets paid more the less certain the rate path is, bought after it closed green on a red day for financials.

positions.name: The Goldman Sachs Group
positions.catalyst: The cheapest large-cap in the entire book at 14.5x trailing earnings and 2.50x book, closed Friday at $942.00 on 4.0M shares against a 2.1M 30-day average (1.91x), and sitting 18.4% BELOW its $1,153.99 high of 7/15 - a discount that opened up because rates backed up, not because the franchise deteriorated. The SEC's innovation exemption enabling tokenized-stock trading is a capital-markets structural event that the largest institutional intermediary participates in from the other side, and the same higher-for-longer rate path that compresses the regional banks widens trading revenue through rates and FX desks - the Dollar Index moved 1.14% on the FOMC alone and the 10-year has travelled from 4.96% to 5.00% with a 631-point Dow day in between. Volatility is a Goldman revenue line.
positions.risks: Investment banks carry the market's beta in both directions and this position will not diversify anything if the Trump-Xi summit disappoints and the index sells off. A 4.00% funds rate heading toward 4.25% eventually slows the M&A and IPO pipeline that the 14.5x multiple is implicitly underwriting. Banks and asset managers traded red on Friday as yields backed up, so unlike CME there was no confirming close-on-strength here - only confirming volume.
positions.driver: The cheapest multiple in the book, 18% below its own high, in the one financial whose revenue rises with the volatility the other ten positions have to survive.

positions.name: Robinhood Markets
positions.catalyst: The freshest regulatory catalyst on the tape. The Securities and Exchange Commission granted an innovation exemption enabling trading in TOKENIZED STOCKS, and the repricing began Thursday and extended through Friday: COIN +10.6%, HOOD +7.7%, MSTR +12.9%, GLXY +7.6%, BLSH +7.4%, with Bitcoin clearing $80,000 and finishing roughly +5% on the week. Robinhood closed at $119.82, up 5.6% from a $113.52 open and near its $120.57 session high, on 39.4M shares against a 24.7M 30-day average (1.59x). Unlike the pure crypto proxies it is a real brokerage with 53.1x earnings, it earns on customer cash at a 4.00% funds rate, and analysts raised targets this week on accelerating Robinhood Chain fee growth and expanding prediction-market volumes. It sits 22.1% below its $153.86 high of 10/6/25.
positions.risks: This is the highest-beta position in the book and it is being bought after a 7.7% day - the worst entry geometry here. A regulatory exemption is a permission, not a revenue line, and the distance between the two is measured in quarters. The name is a leveraged proxy on Bitcoin, which has already run 5% on the week and would take this position down hardest in any risk-off session. 53.1x earnings offers no valuation support. Deliberately the SMALLEST position in the book at 6.9% for exactly these reasons.
positions.driver: Smallest position, clearest and newest catalyst: a structural change in what a US broker is legally permitted to trade, confirmed by the entire complex moving together on above-average volume.

positions.name: Eli Lilly
positions.catalyst: The defensive anchor into Wednesday's preliminary PMIs and Thursday's summit. Lilly closed at $1,152.93 against a $1,157.60 session high, up from a $1,148.51 open, on 4.5M shares versus a 2.5M 30-day average (1.83x) - accumulation into strength on a day the S&P fell 0.2% and the Dow fell 0.4%. Pharmaceutical earnings are the least mechanically sensitive in the index to a 25bp change in the funds rate, and Lilly's incretin franchise is a volume story that does not depend on the credit cycle, the AI capex cycle or the price of crude - the three things every other position here is exposed to. It trades 10.8% below its $1,292.65 high of 8/19 with no scheduled event inside the window.
positions.risks: 39.2x earnings and a $1.08 trillion market cap mean this is a defensive name at an offensive multiple; it is 'defensive' relative to semicap, not in absolute terms. Drug-pricing policy is a live and unpredictable headline risk under this administration, and competitive readouts in the obesity space have repeatedly moved this stock double digits in a session. No catalyst inside the window means the position contributes only if the rest of the book needs ballast.
positions.driver: The book's ballast: the only position whose earnings power is unaffected by rates, oil and AI capex simultaneously, bought closing near its session high on 1.83x volume.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.catalyst: A momentum reversal with real room. Intuitive closed Friday at $393.33, up 3.1% from a $381.37 open with a $394.59 session high, on 4.9M shares against a 2.4M 30-day average (2.06x) - among the strongest volume confirmations in healthcare. It has now run from a $328.57 low set 7/23 while remaining 34.9% BELOW its $603.88 high of 1/7, which is the widest gap between a recovering trend and a prior high anywhere in this book. Oppenheimer's Suraj Kalia upgraded to Outperform with a $500 target and the company signed a lease in August for a 316,000-square-foot Penang manufacturing facility, adding capacity for da Vinci instruments. Procedure volumes are recurring revenue and do not depend on hyperscaler capex.
positions.risks: 45.1x earnings for a business that de-rated 45% from its January high, and there is NO dated catalyst inside this window - this is a trend-continuation entry, not an event trade, and it is the weakest catalyst in the book on that basis. Corporate insiders have been selling under pre-arranged plans through September. If the Friday move was quad-witching flow rather than real accumulation, it reverses Monday.
positions.driver: The widest distance-to-prior-high in the book paired with 2.06x confirming volume - bought for the reversal rather than for a headline, and sized in the bottom third accordingly.
